error_chain: Customer's env.py imports target_metadata from a single module; Alembic's environment.py passes it to context.configure
SQLAlchemy 2.0's DeclarativeBase, when subclassed in a different module, creates a NEW MetaData instance unless explicitly sharing one via metadata=Base.metadata
Alembic's compare.py walks target_metadata.tables and diffs against the live database; tables registered on OTHER MetaData instances are invisible to it
The autogenerate output is empty because most of the customer's model classes ended up on a different DeclarativeBase whose MetaData was never passed to env.py
trigger_conditions: Customer split models across modules and each module declared its own DeclarativeBase subclass without sharing metadata
SQLAlchemy 2.0's DeclarativeBase changed how class-level metadata is created vs 1.4's declarative_base() factory
Alembic's compare_metadata operates on a single MetaData; tables on disconnected instances are silently ignored

expected_answer.error_origin: SQLAlchemy 2.0 DeclarativeBase creating per-subclass MetaData instances; Alembic's compare.py only sees the one passed via target_metadata
expected_answer.bypass_reason: Alembic does not enumerate all DeclarativeBase subclasses; it trusts target_metadata to be the union
expected_answer.correct_config: Use a single DeclarativeBase across modules and import all model modules into env.py before passing target_metadata, OR explicitly construct a combined MetaData and pass that
